messages:
Maya Chen: hey folks — i'm updating our internal incident messaging templates and the on-call handoff checklist. goal is a single small set of canonical snippets we can copy into status pages, customer notes, and internal postmortems. want to lock voice/tone + placeholders today if possible.

Maya Chen: high-level constraints: short customer-facing TL;DR (one sentence), clear impact bullets, what we're doing (in plain english), ETA if we have one, and a short acknow/next steps line. internal sections should include timeline, mitigations tried, live owner, and next steps.

Samir Patel: +1. couple practical bits: add a severity -> page type mapping for language (e.g., Sev1 = "Service interruption affecting multiple customers", Sev2 = "Partial degradation"), and a fallback phrase when ETA unknown: "Investigating; we'll provide an update within X minutes."

Samir Patel: proposed customer status snippet (short):
```
Current status: We are experiencing degraded response times for API requests to the /v1/generate endpoint, affecting approximately 15% of requests.
Impact: Elevated latency and occasional timeouts for real-time features.
What we're doing: Oncall team is investigating routing and autoscaler behavior; engineers are rolling a rollback to the previous model variant.
ETA: Targeting a mitigation within 30 minutes; we'll update sooner if we have progress.
```

Samir Patel: note placeholders: {{service}}, {{endpoint}}, {{impact_scope}}, {{eta_minutes}} — should make templates easy to fill programmatically.

Alex Rivera: love the placeholders. small wording tweak: avoid absolutes like "rolling a rollback" -> "attempting rollback". also prefer proactive empathy line at top for customer copy, e.g., "We're sorry for the disruption" (keep it concise). so final customer opener: "We're investigating an issue impacting {{service}}; apologies for the disruption."

Alex Rivera: for the status page header i suggest structure: 1) short opener, 2) single-sentence impact, 3) what we're doing (1-2 bullets), 4) next update ETA. keeps it scannable.

oncall-bot: Paging: @Maya Chen and @Samir Patel — incident #17825 assigned to maya-chen oncall. Acknowledge with `ack`.

Maya Chen: ack. ran through a quick draft and pasted a combined template below for both external and internal use — please sanity check before i push to ops playbook.

Maya Chen: External status / customer notification template (copyable):
```
[Short opener] We're investigating an issue affecting {{service}}; apologies for the disruption.
[Impact] Users may experience {{impact_scope}} (e.g., delayed responses, timeouts).
[What we're doing] The on-call and engineering teams are actively investigating possible regressions in model routing and autoscaler behavior. Mitigation steps in progress: attempting rollback, increasing capacity, and enabling a warm cache.
[ETA / next update] Next update: within {{eta_minutes}} minutes or sooner.
[Optional guidance] Workaround: If possible, switch to a lower load route (route: {{fallback_route}}) or batch requests.
```

Maya Chen: Internal incident summary template (for channel / postmortem):
```
Summary: Brief one-line summary of user-visible impact.
Severity: Sev{{n}} (reason).
Timeline: bullets with times (HH:MM UTC) and actions.
Mitigations tried: bullet list, include exact commands/configs rolled.
Current status: short line.
Owner(s): @oncall, @engineer.
Next steps: who is doing what in next 15/60 minutes.
Open questions: what gaps we need help with (e.g., logs, metrics). 
Notes: links to traces, deploy IDs, runbooks.
```

Chris O'Neill: adding a short on-call handoff checklist would be useful — especially for shift swaps during long incidents. suggestion:
```
On-call handoff checklist:
- 1-line current status
- What was attempted in last 30 min
- Known blockers (logs/alerts missing, access issues)
- Who owns each next step (name + contact)
- Expected next update time
- Any customer comms scheduled (time + channel)
- Links: status page draft, incident channel, runbook, traces
- If unresolved, escalate path (who to call for infra/ops)
```

Chris O'Neill: also recommend a "language library" with short options for tone: "apologetic" (we're sorry — we're working on it), "informative" (just facts + ETA), "reassuring" (we have rollback plan). pick based on severity and whether there's a workaround.

Samir Patel: one more: add one-liner templates for quick SMS/pager messages where character limits matter. e.g., `API degraded: investigating. Next update in 15m. Owner: @maya-chen`

Maya Chen: perfect. i'll assemble these into a single doc in ops-docs and tag the on-call playbook. after i push i'll ask ops-docs-bot to create a PR description with the templates. please react here with :thumbsup: if you approve or suggest inline edits.

ops-docs-bot: Created draft PR #492: "incident-messaging-templates: add customer + internal templates, handoff checklist" — https://git.internal/repo/pull/492

Alex Rivera: :thumbsup: minor nit — change "Mitigations tried" bullet to include exact timestamps and commands where possible.

Samir Patel: :thumbsup:

Chris O'Neill: :thumbsup: and added note re: escalation phone numbers in the checklist.

Maya Chen: thanks all — i'll merge after addressing alex's timestamp request and will post back here when it's live.

Maya Chen: final note: let's standardize on `{{eta_minutes}}` for customer-facing ETA and `{{update_interval}}` for internal bulletin cadence (e.g., 5m/15m).

Samir Patel: agreed. thanks.
